lruCache.description: LruCache with 500 entries, 5s TTL. ~700K ops/s for get/set, ~680K ops/s for eviction. TTL expiry works correctly.

lineEndingNormalization.description: CRLF→LF conversion is the bottleneck at ~20K ops/s on 500-line files. But per-write overhead is ~0.05ms — negligible for single file operations.

deltaCoalescing.description: Map-based accumulation (Phase 3B) adds ~0.21ms overhead per 1000 deltas vs direct append. The real win is reducing Solid.js store updates from N to 1 per flush interval.

writeNormalization.description: Line ending normalization adds ~0.1ms per write on a 500-line file. For typical dotfiles (<500 lines), overhead is negligible (<0.1ms). The high % overhead is misleading due to 10K iterations.

conclusion: All optimizations have negligible runtime overhead. The real gains are architectural: LRU cache reduces disk I/O for repeated reads, delta coalescing reduces Solid.js re-renders during streaming, line ending normalization prevents mixed-line-ending bugs in dotfiles on Windows.
